reviews.text: My favorite part of the X films is their strong aesthetic vision, and Pearl is no exception—drawing on the appearance of early Technicolor and the melodrama of Douglas Sirk films, it's a delightfully campy pastiche.
reviews.author: Julianne Bell

reviews.text: While I wasn’t blown away by Pearl, I still had a good time and got pretty much what I wanted from it: a deeper understanding of one of the most interesting new horror villains.
reviews.author: Joseph Tomastik

reviews.text: This demented, charming, Wizard of Oz-like horror is all the more disturbing because it doesn’t look like a horror movie.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: Ti West returns to the X film series with his prequel Pearl, a stylish but uneven snapshot of a young woman’s descent into madness.
reviews.author: William Stottor

reviews.text: West and Goth beautifully translate the chilling dichotomy between good and evil with several allusions to The Wizard of Oz, as well as a general nod to the saccharine quality of old Disney films.
reviews.author: Ally Ham

reviews.text: Pearl the character may not be a star, but “Pearl” the movie is an absolute blast!
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Aesthetics aside, a movie like Pearl lives and dies off the lead performance, and Mia Goth delivers a show-stopping performance here.
reviews.author: Shakyl Lambert

reviews.text: Mia Goth dominates the film, given pretty much the entire screen to fill and the runtime to stretch her legs – this is entirely her domain and as Pearl she gives a horror performance for the ages.
reviews.author: Paul Klein

reviews.text: All in all, "Pearl" doesn’t disappoint. While the film’s premise ponders the obsessive ambition and showcases its aftermath, the performances and costume design will impress scene after scene.
reviews.author: Zofia Wijaszka

reviews.text: For someone that loves classic films, there was a lot to admire here. With the lush colors, nods to cinematic history and eccentric characters, this is a film that non-horror audiences would find appreciation for.
reviews.author: Rosalie Kicks

reviews.text: West does a few things better than any director today. It is rare for a movie to show men being afraid before something happens
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: As a prequel, it has some slasher moments that are amplified by Goth's sinister performance as the scream queen in the red dress, but unfortunately it frequents too many common places. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Technically a prequel to his earlier slasher film X (2022), Ti West’s Pearl comfortably stands up on its own as a bold, imaginative, and hugely effective work of horror.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: My X-pectations were too high
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: Ti West’s prequel cements the “X” Cinematic Universe as a force to be reckoned with.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: A mutli-layered exploration of womanhood in relation to exposure and performance.
reviews.author: Savina Petkova

reviews.text: To make all this work Pearl needs a star, and it has it in Goth, whose powerhouse performance elevates what could so easily be a cartoon villain.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: Pearl's journey mimics that of Dorothy from The Wizard of Oz. With a little more blood spatter than glittery shoes.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: You see West making more creative decisions and playing with different scenarios rather than sticking to the same old tricks up his sleeve. He reinvents himself, and with that comes a gem of a horror picture.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: A great horror film that captures the dawning age of cinema beautifully well. Also has a great performance by Mia Goth that deserves all the awards she gets for her performance.
reviews.author: David Griffiths

reviews.text: The result is a successful contrast between a visual language with hints of a fairy tale and a dark story that hides delirium behind the fantasy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniela Urzola

reviews.text: Bathed in a Technicolor that yearns for happiness that will never come, Pearl's red hues enhance the call to the madness of this addictive delirium. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: Instead of lining up the victims and letting Pearl get her Lizzy Borden on, Goth and West ruminate in the age-old debate of nature vs. nurture.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: While Ti West’s X was a smart, sassy homage to The Texas Chainsaw Massacre and other rural horrors from the 1970s, it pales in comparison to the vivid Technicolor 1918 nightmare he and his star Mia Goth have unleashed here.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: For a film with such darkness, violence and pitch-black humour, the visuals of Pearl are a technicolour delight.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: The film is more sumptuously upholstered than most exercises in kitsch, closer to David Lynch than John Waters, with one of those wraparound musical scores that feels like a mink coat.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Pearl wants so badly to be a star. Part of the film’s pleasure lies in realising that Goth already is.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: I'm quite sure no animals were harmed in the making of this film, but many of those farmyard critters don't make it out alive...
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: A savvy deepening and recontextualising of a must-see scary-movie franchise that's as much about desire, dreams and determination as notching up deaths.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Goth is riotously entertaining throughout, but two specific scenes, in both of which the camera rests solely on her face for an extended shot, capture the full force of her unnerving talent.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: She slashes, stabs and decapitates aplenty, and proves a dab hand with a pitchfork. That’s essentially the film. It’s Judy Garland goes rogue on a farm.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Goth’s energy, focus and commitment here is extraordinary.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: This prequel to the much-admired 2022 slasher X is turbocharged by a gloriously bonkers performance by Mia Goth. Seriously, it's one of the best acting jobs you'll see this year -- a top hat-wearing, liquid morphine-guzzling, monologue-unleashing triumph.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: Pearl’s torment is believable largely because Goth single-handedly wills it to be. Her commitment to every choked cry for attention, to every glassy-eyed departure from reality, is unimpeachable.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Pearl exists primarily as a savage and silly showcase for the utterly luminous Goth, who sinks her acting teeth into the myriad tones and vibes of the character.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: From the opening credits with their cursive retro font to the end crawl that plays over Goth making a deranged face, the film harks back to vintage B-movies about crazed young ladies...
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: Fresh, subversive and drenched in delicious irony and dark humour. Goth continues to impress.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Genre cinema performed at the top of its game, Pearl is a masterclass in just about everything. If you’re one of the few that hasn’t yet sought out Pearl by other means, your patience is about to be very richly rewarded.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: It’s mad, bad and sad and will leave you wondering how it’s possible to root for this demonic diamond — or Pearl — in the rough.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: This tenderly perverse Cinderella story functions just as well all on its own, and in some respects hovers outside of time, as a parable about cinema in general
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Pearl is notable as a pandemic film... though much like its engagement with sex, violence and entertainment, and its treatment of women, the film sets the table for a discussion but doesn’t quite make a full meal of it.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: ... An American gothic shocker with a lot to say — and an awards-worthy lead performance from Mia Goth.
reviews.author: Kim Newman

reviews.text: Pearl is brutal, emotionally satisfying and horrifying, in all the best ways.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: A new-wave horror chiller that clocks in as an absolute knockout exercise in top-tier terror; a cliche-averse, outside-the-box prequel to X, the trip skillfully blends old-school movie trappings with a laser-sharp edge
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: As nubile worry Pearl, Mia Goth is a textbook definition of torment.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: Goth’s powerhouse performance is shot through with both a mischievous and desperately sad giddiness that never lets up.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: Ti West’s brilliantly bonkers new film Pearl, for instance, would be unthinkable without Mia Goth.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: One to chalk up to that small but delightful sub-genre of retro slasher weepies.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: Separately, X and Pearl might not have made my 10 Best of 2022 list; together, how could they not?
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The result doesn't quite stand up on its own, but as an eye-catching origins story that casts new light on the original film, it's a malevolent marvel.
reviews.author: Matt Glasby

reviews.text: An amazing technicolour nightmare.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: The film is very similar to its titular protagonist: pure unprejudiced extreme. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Boetti

reviews.text: Ti West confirms that his cinematographic horror plan has life and that he can draw upon distinct nuances without being repetitive. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Adrián Monserrat

reviews.text: … beautifully shot, but deeply ugly… Mia Goth is definitely a star.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: Pearl feels like an acting exercise: some performers need to know a character's backstory before incarnating it. Pearl turns this exploration into a somewhat redundant story that seems to only exist to showcase Goth's talents. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hernán Ferreirós

reviews.text: Pearl has everything it takes to become a horror classic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Pearl is a masterclass of horror filmmaking with a powerful ending, but it relies on a familiarity with the franchise that holds it back.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: It isn’t your standard horror film, and the movie is better for it. While some filmmakers could ease their foot off the pedal for their second round, West keeps his engaged to the floor here.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: It's a hypnotic, shattering performance that rings of emotional truth.
reviews.author: Santanu Das

reviews.text: ...as if Dorothy got sucked up by a tornado and dropped down in The Texas Chain Saw Massacre — holding the chainsaw.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Pearl provides a surprisingly tender origin story for its titular character.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: It shows how little has changed for women seeking autonomy despite sixty years passing, but it never truly delves deeper than motive. Goth is great (that monologue) and the style homages are fun, but that's about it for me.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Director Ti West's disturbing horror film begins and ends with the unhinged and genuinely scary performance of Mia Goth.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: Goth is phenomenal and worthy of award season praise by making Pearl a devastating character and a standout in the genre as she’s not quite the Final Girl we’re used to.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: PEARL is a vicious fairyland strewn with the wreckage of one very tender and broken soul. It is filled with the sweeping shots and vibrant colors of a Douglas Sirk melodrama.
reviews.author: Dolores Quintana

reviews.text: Prequels, like Ti West’s new film Pearl, come bearing an existential mandate—you need audiences that will revere the previous film, and a compelling reason to backtrack in the story, to find out how its rich narrative materials came to be.
reviews.author: Michael Atkinson

reviews.text: A candy-colored, nightmarish dream world of lofty ambitions, brutal violence, and bloody murder creates a Golden Age of Hollywood horror movie that’s unlike any other.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Pearl is definitely one of the most memorable movies of 2022
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Holy mother of Pearl, this is one perilous journey steeped in maniacal misery.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: A beautiful slow-burn thriller with an unnerving performance by Mia Goth.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Redefines the genre showing that horror can happen in unlikely bright places. Mia Goth’s well deserved starring role.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: It is worth it for X fans to check out this prequel with a lot of dark ideas — many of which are executed superbly. Between the two movies, this is the one you’ll be less likely to rewatch, but it works as a decent prequel.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: When X came out it easily fell into the thriller sub-genre of horror movies building the suspense until the third act. Pearl, on the other had, was more of a drama that turned into a gory, slasher film.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Pearl is a compelling and sinister intro to the character established earlier in the year, taken to new heights by Mia Goth’s striking performance.
reviews.author: Kristy Strouse

reviews.text: What makes Pearl surprisingly brilliant compared to X, is that in reality it is a profound drama with slasher elements, not the other way around.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: This was pretty great. Like that last shot, it’s going to linger. How could it not?
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: ... A bleak yet colourful character study which enriches and gives texture to the world of X.
reviews.author: Joel Harley

reviews.text: Mia Goth shines in 'Pearl', Ti West's companion piece to this year's 'X', delivering one of the most memorable horror performances of the year.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: [Mia] Goth knows this character through and through; every glimmer in her eye, every sinister inkling of her true character, every revelatory word. Pearl is Goth’s dance, and she fills the stage better than a whole troupe in Palace Follies.
reviews.author: Kimberley Elizabeth

reviews.text: Between Tyler Bates’ vintage-inspired score, West’s clever cinematography, and Goth’s staggering performance, Pearl is a gripping character drama disguised as a horror movie, and a compelling prequel that strengthens an already-impressive story.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: ...a hit-and-miss endeavor that’d hardly be worth mentioning were it not for Goth’s eye-opening, star-making turn.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: West’s bold, stylish direction and brilliant use of color and shadow push Pearl into a whole different level of horror. Goth carries the picture with a bit of acting that is subtle and over-the-top at the same time.
reviews.author: Bobby LePire

reviews.text: Fantastic touches like a fantasy dance sequence, the tribute to the 1918 movie era and the atmosphere of Pearl’s world are countered by the usual horror film stuff that must have stab-kill-gore elements. Ti West does knows how to smash the horror genre.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Goth’s Pearl may be a tragicomic creation, but she takes her dreams seriously, which serves as a bulwark against the synthetic glibness that might have creeped into the film.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: While X remains the stronger film, Pearl has enough to stand on its own and it's a stunning showcase for Mia Goth, particularly *that* monologue and those closing credits.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: I'll certainly be seeing the other chapters of this creepy saga. I will, however, not let my children grow up around pitchforks. Lesson learned there.
reviews.author: Tobias Jeg

reviews.text: It’s a pretty inspired way to deliver an origin story.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: West and Goth will continue to build their collaboration in the future. They’ve become horror’s latest great pairing, following in the footsteps of Craven and Campbell.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Goth would be recognized by awards bodies everywhere if people who cared about movie awards watched movies like 'Pearl.'
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: This fantasy adventure quickly spirals into a nightmare highlighting the juxtaposition between the world Pearl envisions for herself and the reality she inhabits.
reviews.author: Jenn Adams

reviews.text: 'Pearl' is a surprisingly humorous, macabre tale about a woman's sinister rampage. Mia Goth deserves an Oscar.
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: Pearl is the perfect companion piece to X, scratching an entirely different itch than its grimy predecessor.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: Pearl is an unsettling homage to a long-lost era, with Mia Goth's incredible central performance bringing American Psycho vibes to a small town.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: It’s heartening to see such a clear-eyed aesthetic that seems so right for our times.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: West and Goth created an inventive, unique slasher genre, and a movie worth rewatching several times.
reviews.author: Maxwell Rabb

reviews.text: The result never fully rises above the pack, but it’s still passable.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Much of 'Pearl' predicates itself on the action chops of Goth, who takes the character to another level in how she changes emotions
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: It’s barely 90 minutes long, but it feels so much longer in practice.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: What is clear is Goth’s deep and impressive immersion here, projecting broad emotions and conveying persona changeups on a dime.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: If you happen to exist in the tiny Venn diagram overlap of people who love horror and the glossy aesthetic of Douglas Sirk movies, get to the theater. West has made your Citizen Kane, and Goth could be your long-shot pick for an Oscar.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Ti West and Mia Goth have taken the groundwork for a deeper exploration of the parallels between loneliness and madness when driven with the promise of fame while drenched in the façade of the Technicolor dream factory.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: You leave admiring the film’s kills, the lingua franca of any slasher flick. What stays with you, though, is its portrait of a psychological crack turning into a chasm.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Ti West pulls off a remarkable feat by taking an origins story that would usually end up as a short in the extras of the home release and stretches it into a full-length feature that keeps the audience engaged thanks to Mia Goth’s obsessive performance.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: This prequel to X promises an origin story, and while it may leave off with more questions than answers, it's still a well-crafted gore-fest and a vivid character study.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: A seemingly simple horror film that reveals itself to be richly textured both on and below the surface.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: This is, above all things, Mia Goth's movie... it is wonderful character work, and worthy of having a film built around it.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Co-screenwriter and star Mia Goth’s Baby Jane/Norma Desmond rictus grins and disarming naturalism make it hard to root against Pearl, and the playful but never jokey film draws strength from the persistent dread roused by our darkest fears.
reviews.author: Jay Horton

reviews.text: An entertainingly nasty tale about the birth of a killer.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Simultaneously gorgeous and horrifying — much like Pearl herself.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Mia Goth is the reason to see this. She's worthy of every award and accolade possible. Again, a bit too much of a pastiche, albeit a different kind than X, but the central performance (particularly a monologue) is what makes this a cut above the rest.
reviews.author: Jim Laczkowski

reviews.text: Feeling like a deranged mix of Wizard of Oz—there is even a scarecrow scene—meets Texas Chainsaw Massacre, Pearl combines a fantasy feel with a riveting turn with Mia Goth as Pearl and shocking bloodshed.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: Anticlimactic and in search of a real hook outside of its relationship to its superior predecessor.
reviews.author: Charles Lyons-Burt

reviews.text: Mia Goth is eating up every single moment in this one, and her monologue is fantastic. Ti West’s editing and pure showcase of style is on another level here.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Pearl manages to be that rare prequel that does nothing but enhance and enrich its counterpart. Ti West somehow manages to craft a Gone With the Wind prelude to Texas Chainsaw Massacre while Mia Goth gives a terrifying Oscar-deserving performance.
reviews.author: Cody Leach

reviews.text: If Douglas Sirk made a slasher flick, it would be Pearl.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Incredibly effective, flawlessly acted, and works as both a standalone piece and as part of a whole. Tense, gripping and sometimes shocking, the movie comes in as one of the better horror experiences I’ve had this year.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Pearl is too twisted and weird for all viewers. But it's more accomplished than X and it allows Goth to smear the screen with blood, unleashed rage, and a killer smile -- or maybe I should say, a killer’s smile.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It’s certainly a worthy prequel.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: West and Goth have expanded on the first installment’s tale of sexual repression as violence in this deranged feature that’s elevated even further by Goth’s sparkling and wistful performance as a ruthless killer.
reviews.author: Lindsay Traves

reviews.text: Pearl is a gift.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Pearl is a rather unusual companion piece to Ti West's X that you can't ever look away from.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Because Mia Goth is so good, Pearl's descent into madness feels especially tragic.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Watch Pearl for Mia Goth. She is great and she knows it.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Creepy and surprisingly moving with Hitchcockian suspense. Mia Goth gives one of the best performances of her career.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Pearl enhances everything that made X special while being a film that is exceptionally different from its predecessor.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: I love that Pearl feels so different than X, as it should be. It's not made up of the same story ingredients. It's a character study, akin to Joker. Like Joker, Pearl boasts an undeniable performance by Mia Goth (Oscar pay attention).
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: Goth delivers an electrifying and truly scary performance.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Goth makes the most of a croaking, lengthy one-take monologue, during which a new horror monster is born. Pearl is the rare origin story where you see the breakdown happening in real time.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: Ladies and gentlemen, the world of horror has a new scream queen. Her name is Mia Goth.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: Pearl is plenty of fun, without a doubt... However, knowing a lot about a genre is one thing. Being able to say something substantive about it is quite another.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Ti West has cottoned on to Goth's greatness, bless him, and given her the demented showcase her talent's long deserved and cried out for. And she kills it, pun intended
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Pearl won't convert anyone who didn’t like X, but if you’re already on board, this horror movie is a great continuation. Mia Goth is captivating and it's clear why she has become director Ti West's muse - you cannot tear your eyes away from her.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: X was a fairly standard horror, well executed (ahem) without breaking the mould. But Pearl is if anything a little better in every respect, thanks in part to a creepy central performance by Goth.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Pearl is a beautiful follow-up to such a down-and-dirty horror film, moving and unsettling, perfectly showcasing Ti West’s talents as a filmmaker.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Pearl gets a little too close to letting you simply laugh at her. We know she wouldn’t like that.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: Put Carrie White into The Wizard of Oz, basically — but make sure she's seen Mulholland Drive.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Goth imbues Pearl with an almost unheard of depth and sadness that will make you feel legitimate empathy for this creature that is harboring an unawakened evil.
reviews.author: Dan Tabor

reviews.text: While [Pearl] might not be another blast of genre thrills at the same level [as X], it still functions as a self-contained piece of genre filmmaking and a terrific showcase for its lead actress.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: Bloody remarkable!
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Pearl is a surprisingly self-contained film, it can be enjoyed in a vacuum, but it works even better as a companion piece to X.
reviews.author: Michelle Kisner

reviews.text: Combining a fabulous visual aesthetic with a delightfully unhinged central performance and some spectacular gore moments, this is an unabashed genre treat that’s full of surprises.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: While not as horrific, Pearl does let Mia Goth shine brighter in her role. The prequel doesn't capture the same magic as X but instead carves out its own dream.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: Pearl may legitimately be one of the best-looking films of the year.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: Pearl isn’t particularly suspenseful, but that’s by design: It’s a perversion of the small-town-girl follies of Old Hollywood melodramas, scented with the copper aroma of blood.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: It doesn’t pack the same wallop that “X” did or feature a memorable death by crocodile, but Goth makes a meal out of the character who at one point delivers a no-holds-bar five-minute, all timer monologue.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: 'Pearl’ stands as a gorgeous three-tier cake, but beneath its colorful exterior lays a product that prides style above substance.
reviews.author: Josh Korngut

reviews.text: A super-stylized shocker with a wild, freakishly compelling story—about how mental illness and instability can turn almost anyone into a monster.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: There’s no denying anything about Goth’s performance here, which is fearless, revealing, and harrowing.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: Mia Goth’s performance is terrific, which is good because it’s what most of the film rides on, along with its era-appropriate quirks.
reviews.author: Jenni Miller

reviews.text: [Pearl is] gloriously demented and Mia Goth proves here that she truly is one of the most fascinating performers working today.
reviews.author: Heather Wixson

reviews.text: Lurking over it is our knowledge that Pearl is going to eventually begin killing some people. It works really well as an origin story, all held together by a tour de force performance from Mia Goth.
reviews.author: Eric Goldman

reviews.text: “Pearl” is well made and has a terrific central performance by Goth, but it’s still a lurid slasher movie with arthouse pretensions.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: "Pearl proves that A24’s first horror franchise is Mia Goth, who pulls double duty once again in a movie that manages to out-perform the original in nearly every way."
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: Mia Goth is brilliant here. It’s a performance that balances unhinged craziness with pure innocence.
reviews.author: JimmyO

reviews.text: A genuinely creepy horror. West chooses methodic movements rather than jump scares to terrify the audience. And he never loses the movie’s underlying sense of humour that is as clever as it is demented.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: In this prequel to director Ti West’s 2022 horror flick X, Mia Goth shows why she is one of the all-time great actresses in horror movies. Her disturbing performance as the title character in Pearl is a master class in horror excellence.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: West, one of the genre’s true artisans of sticky dread, certainly has fun seeding a handsomely mounted and shot (by Eliot Rockett) period melodrama with the trappings of imminent violence...
reviews.author: Robert Abele

reviews.text: A slow burn — the setting is known as Powder Keg Farms for a reason — and it builds to a riotous climax as Goth guides viewers every loopy, daffy step of the way.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: With Pearl, writer-director Ti West both embraces and elevates what horror movies can do, in a way that further solidifies his standing as one of the best things to ever happen to the genre.
reviews.author: Phil Pirrello

reviews.text: It’s... a bit thin and undercooked, but Goth’s performance transcends its limits.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: It has the ability to reach new heights of self-reflexive pleasure but settles instead for pastiche that, while well-crafted, feels lifeless and devoid of true feeling.
reviews.author: Sarah-Tai Black

reviews.text: Pearl, in a neat link to its predecessor, cheekily acknowledges that the magic of the movies can be plenty dangerous, too.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: So much is missing, from the religious fixation to the voracious libido, I feel like a completely different movie was made for a completely different franchise. Someone forgot this was a horror movie.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: Pearl completely upends any expectations for what a horror film can look and feel like. [Mia] Goth, who also co-wrote Pearl with West, is nothing short of a revelation here.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: Pearl is a loving homage to early Hollywood films, from the sweeping score to the bathed-in-Technicolor nightmare.
reviews.author: Sarah Jane

reviews.text: Since we know where its title character winds up, PEARL works not so much as a suspenseful thriller but as a character study dependent on its central performance, in which its star delivers in spades.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: This is the Ti West we’ve been waiting for, a filmmaker who knows his history, understands style, and exploits both to his and the audience’s benefit.
reviews.author: J Hurtado

reviews.text: "Pearl" is more character study than slasher flick—though there is a lot of blood. More "Leave Her to Heaven" less "Texas Chain Saw Massacre."
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: [W]e know exactly what's coming, and in terms of the specifics that might not be clear, the big question is whether or not we want or even need to know those details.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Pearl makes for a vastly different viewing experience from X thanks to its drastic shifts in style, tone, and cinematic influences, but with enough connective tissue to enrich its predecessor.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: Pearl is a fever dream of choreographed dancing, decapitations and Mia Goth carrying the weight of all 100+ minutes.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Pearl adds an important piece of the puzzle to this horror trilogy that West has been creating, and I hope this gets people to see Goth as a bonafide actor with her amazing performances in the first two films.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: There are unpleasant moments, but this is an homage to the heightened melodramas of the 1950s and 60s. But with more axes, scarecrow sex and hungry alligators than Douglas Sirk could ever have imagined.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: The film fails to deliver the scares its increasingly ominous atmosphere promises.
reviews.author: Olivia McCormack

reviews.text: While Goth was very good in X, she functioned as part of a larger ensemble and didn’t really stand out. In Pearl, however, she is the movie.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Pearl is a film with undeniable style, but questionable substance.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Mia Goth plays a woman desperate to be a star but doomed never to be one. The irony is that Pearl should be the movie that propels Goth herself to proper stardom. She's simply sensational.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: A showcase for the considerable talent of Mia Goth. She reprises her role as Pearl and delivers an unforgettable performance.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: If X was Ti West‘s homage to classic 70’s horror effort The Texas Chainsaw Massacre, then Pearl could almost be aligned with The Wizard of Oz, just with, you know, a lot more blood and dry-humping scarecrows.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Pearl is ultimately an empty exercise in style masquerading as a character study, and for as fantastic as Mia Goth is, her performance mostly succeeds at making Ti West’s homages just a little bit easier to stomach.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: Pearl is the film that cements Goth as one of the most interesting Scream Queens right now. She is a tour-de-force with the ability to captivate us through her craft, even as she is stepping into a vicious character.
reviews.author: Sabrina Ramirez

reviews.text: Pearl works as a standalone horror movie; the contrast between The Wizard of Oz vibe and the lurking dread builds a wonderful kind of tension and makes the moments of bloodshed hit that much harder.
reviews.author: Andrew Webster

reviews.text: "...it's a haunting, blackly comic melodrama, a Disney Princess movie for axe murderers, that's just as unforgettable as the sleazy slasher vibes of X."
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: It’s chilling and even moving at times, thanks to Goth’s incredible performance. The story makes some mistakes, but the actress is flawless.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Ultimately, Pearl is a unique and successful slasher prequel. It does something truly noteworthy in the genre: making a big swing through its melodrama-meets-slasher formula and hitting it out of the park.
reviews.author: Alejandra Martinez

reviews.text: West celebrates what folks love about campy horror films without looking down on the material.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: With this film, Pearl has solidified herself as one of the most iconic killers such as Freddy Kruger and Michael Myers.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Mia Goth is so mesmerizing you can’t take your eyes off of her.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: A fine vehicle for a bravura Mia Goth performance. There's just enough surrounding her to get viewers through the movie, but she is the reason it exists.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: It promises to give viewers more insight about Pearl, but the execution is underwhelming & the film’s message muddled, uncertain of its message.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: This new installment stands on its own unsettlingly odd merits.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Taken together, “X” and “Pearl” make for a compelling double-feature showcasing blood-spattered homages to different eras of film.
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: The final results are a more discordant companion piece than one would expect, but plenty to appreciate for what it attempts to analyze.
reviews.author: Josh Parham

reviews.text: Mia Goth is astonishing, eliciting empathy despite the character’s insanity; Pearl is as thematically rich as X, if not more so. Both are the definition of master-class horror
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: its embrace of the glorious, super-saturated Technicolor movies of Hollywood’s golden age is simply stunning, its “Wizard of Oz” references cheeky and Goth’s performance rigorously unbalanced.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: If Mia Goth isn’t at least in contention for some kind of acting award this year, between both X and Pearl, then there really is a problem.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: It’s a thrill to behold something so self-possessed, something that manages to be both wholly reminiscent and, in aggregate, truly singular.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: From its anachronistic homages to its tensionless filmmaking, Pearl doesn’t have nearly as much to say as its predecessor. Mia Goth gives it her all as a villainess who dreams of stardom, but the film can’t decide what to do with her.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Pearl is a Golden Age Hollywood narrative that unravels into a captivating yet nightmarish trip about love and sickness.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Pearl proves that both Ti West and Mia Goth continue to be powerhouses in the genre space in this technicolor terror.
reviews.author: Patrick Cavanaugh

reviews.text: At its heart, Goth is fabulous, switching from her sweet-and-sunny persona to full-on raging diva.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: West is having fun. Lurid fun, yes, but fun nonetheless. And if you’re a fan of horror and filmmaking, you will, too.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Goth's amazing performance is what makes this slasher film so precious.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Pearl’s potent pastiche of a woman’s weepie with a slow-burning slasher feels fresh and exciting to watch unfold.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

reviews.text: “Pearl” is the superior of the two heavily-stylized slashers, partly because it dedicates so much time to building the eponymous antiheroine from the ground up.
reviews.author: Jack King

reviews.text: A Mia Goth tour de force. Another A+ chapter in Ti West's celebration of cinema and exploration of the gnawing devastation of rejection and having dreams out of reach ... and in Pearl's case, the violence and chaos that can spark.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Mia Goth delivers her best performance yet.
reviews.author: Lex Briscuso

reviews.text: Those who found something to like in the strangely sex-negative X might get something out of this. Or you could just watch an actually good film about ambition and obsession...
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: “Pearl” does hold up on its own, a fun-house-mirror “Imitation of Life” full of insider winks to horror classics...
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: A working knowledge of X isn’t required to enjoy the stylish bloodbath that follows. But sly parallels lurk everywhere...
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: A gruesome portrait of another young woman hungering for a life greater than the fate she’s been handed, it makes an amusing companion piece to X.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: It’s an impressive feat of filmmaking, but one that reveals nothing new, a major misstep for a film seemingly dedicated to doing just that.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: Perhaps I shouldn’t have enjoyed Pearl as much as I did: but it’s clever, limber, gruesome and brutally well acted. A gem.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Pearl does end up enhancing X a little bit by essentially chronicling all the shortcomings and repression that drove Pearl mad. But it’s not without its own shortcomings. Chiefly, that it isn’t remotely scary.
reviews.author: Brian Formo

reviews.text: More than just a fantastic prequel: it successfully illuminates and recontextualizes its predecessor, dramatically improving a film that was already acclaimed to begin with.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

synopsis: Filmmaker Ti West returns with another chapter from the twisted world of X, in this astonishing follow-up to the year's most acclaimed horror film. Trapped on her family's isolated farm, Pearl must tend to her ailing father under the bitter and overbearing watch of her devout mother. Lusting for a glamorous life like she's seen in the movies, Pearl finds her ambitions, temptations, and repressions all colliding in this stunning, technicolor-inspired origin story of X's iconic villain.
